elements.quote: This is the second version (first update) of the living systematic review, replacing the previous version (available as a data supplement).
elements.reason: The manuscript identifies itself as an update and refers to the previous version, addressing the conditional requirement for updates to identify prior reviews, but the full rationale context linking to the previous review is not retrieved.
No retrieved evidence briefly describes the proposed mechanism of action of the prophylactic interventions (e.g., drugs, antibodies, vitamins).
The review evaluates individual prophylactic drugs/antibodies in randomised trials, which are not complex interventions or complex delivery contexts, so a logic model requirement does not apply.
No retrieved evidence contains an explicit statement of the review objective(s) or question(s). The evidence covers registration, search, selection, and methods, but not a stated objective.

Although this is a review of intervention effects (prophylaxis NMA), no retrieved evidence reports planned comparisons framed using PICO or a variant; only implicit eligibility hints exist (e.g., 'people at risk of covid-19 were allocated to prophylaxis or no prophylaxis'), which do not constitute an explicit statement of planned comparisons.

elements.quote: We included randomised trials of people at risk of covid-19 that compared drugs, therapeutic doses of vitamins, or antibodies for prophylaxis against one another or against no prophylaxis (placebo or standard care, as defined by the researchers)... We included studies addressing people pre- or post-exposure to covid-19 and at low risk (e.g. unexposed community member) or high risk (e.g. member of the same household with one or more positive cases, contact of index case, healthcare worker or long term care resident) for covid-19.
elements.reason: Eligibility characteristics are clearly specified: study design (randomised trials), population (people at risk of covid-19, low/high risk groups), interventions/comparators (drugs, vitamins, antibodies vs each other or no prophylaxis), and settings (pre- or post-exposure).

elements.quote: with no restriction on language of publication
elements.reason: Language restriction is explicitly addressed (none). Publication status is partially addressed by exclusion of press-releases-only trials (text_13) and inclusion of preprints, but no dissemination year restriction is stated in the retrieved evidence.

elements.quote: 54 Randomised trial with no results

elements.quote: compared drugs, therapeutic doses of vitamins, or antibodies for prophylaxis against one another or against no prophylaxis (placebo or standard care, as defined by the researchers)

elements.quote: We excluded randomised trials published only as press releases and trials that evaluated vaccination, nutrition, and non-drug supportive care interventions.
elements.reason: Notable exclusions (vaccination, nutrition, non-drug supportive care, press-release-only trials) are listed but no rationale for these restrictions is provided in the retrieved evidence.

elements.quote: across the following domains: bias arising from the randomisation process; bias owing to departures from the intended intervention; bias from missing outcome data; bias in measurement of the outcome; bias in selection of the reported results, including deviations from the registered protocol; bias due to competing risks; and bias arising from early termination for benefit

elements.quote: used a revision of the Cochrane tool for assessing risk of bias in randomised trials (RoB 2.0) 19 to rate trials at i) low risk of bias, ii) some concerns-probably low risk of bias, iii) some concerns-probably high risk of bias, or iv) high risk of bias

elements.quote: We summarised the effect of prophylactic drugs on laboratory confirmed infection and on laboratory confirmed, suspected, and probable infection using odds ratios (ORs) and corresponding 95% credible intervals (CrIs). Due to low number of events in most studies, we summarised all other dichotomous outcomes using risk differences (RDs) and corresponding 95% credible intervals (CrIs).
elements.reason: The Summary Measures section specifies the effect measure (OR for infection outcomes, RD for all other dichotomous outcomes) for each outcome type.

elements.quote: Pending data from quantitative studies of patient values, we chose thresholds of small but important effects of 0.1% for mortality; 2% for adverse events leading to discontinuation and laboratory confirmed infection; 3% for suspected, probable, or laboratory confirmed infection; and 1% for admission to hospital.
elements.reason: Thresholds for interpreting effect size (small but important effects) are reported for each outcome along with the rationale (pending patient values data).

elements.quote: To facilitate interpretation of the results, we calculated absolute effects for laboratory confirmed infection and suspected, probable, and laboratory confirmed infection-outcomes that were summarised as ORs. We used the median event rate in the standard care or placebo arms to calculate the baseline risk.
elements.reason: The method for re-expressing OR results as absolute effects (using median event rate in control arms as baseline risk) is described.

elements.quote: Due to low number of events in most studies, we summarised all other dichotomous outcomes using risk differences (RDs)
elements.reason: The choice of risk differences is justified by the low number of events in most studies; the use of ORs for infection outcomes is implied by the NMA framework.

elements.quote: Eight randomised trials addressing ramipril, 41 bromhexine hydrochloride, 51 ... were excluded ... from the network meta-analysis because they each enrolled less than [two] arm. Since the molecule, rather than drug dose or duration of use, dictates the choice of nodes, the two active treatment arms in one three-arm trial were combined (hydroxychloroquine once weekly or twice weekly). 35
